sections.overview: *Lipogenys gillii* is a rarely seen deep-sea fish originally described from the western North Atlantic. Modern fish catalogues place it in Notacanthidae, although older works treated *Lipogenys* as its own family.
sections.identification: Its distinctive sucker-like mouth is one feature separating it from related deep-sea fishes.
sections.habitat: It lives on the seabed, recorded at about 600–2,000 m off Atlantic Canada and the United States. A specimen has also been confirmed from the Hawaiian Archipelago, but its full distribution remains unresolved.
sections.diet: It draws sediment into its sucker-like mouth and feeds mainly on the organic material it contains.
sections.behavior: It is rarely encountered, and many aspects of its biology remain poorly known.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted provide too little species-specific information to describe its reproduction reliably.
sections.ecology: A second species in the genus, *Lipogenys hyalinumvelum*, was described from Portugal in 2024; its translucent gill-cover flap distinguishes it from *L. gillii*.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports no IUCN Red List evaluation for this species; lack of assessment is not evidence that it faces no risk.
